name: ECOncrete bio-enhancing concrete armoring installations in Israel
place: Haifa Bay ("Polinom" port breakwater), Herzliya Marina, Jaffa Port; also reported at a Haifa naval base, Ashdod port and Eilat port (dates not found)
type: bio-enhancing precast concrete armoring units, seawall panels, and tide pools (Antifer-shaped armor units at Haifa; seawall face panels at Herzliya; tide-pool units at Jaffa)
purpose: ecological enhancement (biodiversity, native-species dominance, water purification) of coastal/port infrastructure that would otherwise be built in plain Portland-cement concrete; secondary claimed benefit of 'bioprotection' reducing structural maintenance

year_built.haifa_polinom_breakwater: port constructed 2012; ECOncrete units deployed and monitored 2013-2015 (some company material says 2013-2016) [R1][R2]
year_built.herzliya_marina_seawall: November 2014, monitored to at least 22 months post-deployment (~Sept 2016), company field says 'ongoing' [R2]

status: Haifa/Polinom: 24-month comparative study completed 2015, units presumed still in place (unconfirmed). Herzliya: described as ongoing. Jaffa: installed 2019, no later status update found.

dimensions.haifa_polinom: exact unit count/breakwater length not confirmed in primary case-study text (one earlier AI-summarized fetch of the same page said '15 units' but this is unverified against the full PDF) [R1][R2]
dimensions.herzliya: monitoring used a 30x30 cm quadrat frame; total seawall area/unit count not found [R2]

cost.per_unit_or_project: not found for any Israeli site
cost.cost_premium_vs_standard_concrete: approximately 2-7% more than standard marine concrete mixes, per company [R8]
cost.company_funding_not_project_cost: $5M Series A led by Bridges Israel + RElab, announced 2020-06-09 [R13]; earlier ~$1M and ~$3M raises reported only by article title, full text blocked (HTTP 403) [R8]

designer: ECOncrete Tech Ltd. (Tel Aviv, Israel), founded 2012 by Dr. Shimrit Perkol-Finkel (CEO) and Dr. Ido Sella (CTO), both marine ecologists [R7][R11][R13]

financed_by.jaffa_port: Atarim Group (Tel Aviv-Yafo municipal coastline development corporation) [R5]
financed_by.haifa_polinom: not found (not confirmed to be Israel Ports Development & Assets Company)
financed_by.herzliya_marina: not found (not confirmed to be Marina Herzliya Ltd.)

motivation: Company founded on the argument that standard concrete coastal infrastructure is ecologically poor habitat (chemistry, smooth texture, steep incline vs natural rock); each Israeli site was a pilot/retrofit opportunity arising from other parties' construction or eco-branding goals (Haifa: side-by-side comparison during new port construction; Herzliya: Blue Flag eco-marina retrofit; Jaffa: Atarim Group innovation trial framed by port ecologist Rotem Trabitzky as balancing conservation and development) [R1][R2][R5][R6]
outcome: Haifa: >2x invertebrate species richness/biodiversity vs standard Antifer units, greater fish diversity, ~2/3 native species on ECOncrete vs invasive-dominated on standard units [R1][R2]. Herzliya: at 22 months, diverse invertebrate colonization on ECOncrete units vs a control that declined BELOW its own original baseline [R2]. Jaffa: no quantified result found, only qualitative ecologist commentary [R6]. No structural/wave-attenuation/storm-performance data found for any site - all outcome data is ecological only.
disambiguation_resolved: This project's own discovery sweep (discovery_israel.md) flagged the 'Haifa Port pilot' and the 'Bay Port/Polinom installation' as possibly the same site described inconsistently. This dossier's direct read of ECOncrete's full case-study PDF (which names the site 'Polinom Port - Haifa' throughout, construction year 2012) resolves this: they are the SAME installation, not two distinct sites.
relation_to_master_list: seeded from 02_research/01_targets.md row econcrete-armoring-israel (Section D 'New Israel topics'), compiled from discovery_israel.md items 12-15
relevance_to_haifa_reef_proposal: Direct same-bay precedent: Haifa/Polinom pilot is in Haifa Bay itself and shows ECOncrete-style armor units can be fabricated, installed and monitored on Haifa Bay port infrastructure with measured ecological uplift. Core transferable idea: use bio-enhancing armor units as the FACING MATERIAL of a Haifa reef/breakwater structure (drop-in substitute for standard cube antifers already used in Israeli port construction). Does NOT transfer: none of the Israeli case studies measured wave attenuation, surfability, or storm-structural performance - all outcome data is ecological only, so a Haifa surf-reef proposal still needs separate hydrodynamic/structural design work.
